nodes.name: Sundri
nodes.desc: The tree that gives the Sundarbans its name. UNESCO-listed forest descriptions and Wikipedia note it is very sensitive to rising salinity.

nodes.name: Gewa
nodes.desc: A salt-tolerant mangrove tree that grows alongside sundri, goran and keora in the tidal forest.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae in the tidal channels. They feed zooplankton and filter-feeding fish and shrimp.

nodes.name: Fiddler crabs
nodes.desc: Burrowing crabs that sift mud for algae, microbes and detritus. Many predators hunt them, and they rework the sediment as they feed.

nodes.name: Shrimp
nodes.desc: Young shrimp shelter among mangrove roots, and the forest supports commercial shrimp and crab catches.

nodes.name: Spotted deer (chital)
nodes.desc: The main large prey of the Sundarbans tiger. Browses and grazes on the forest floor.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots through mud and leaf litter. Listed among the tiger's prey in the Sundarbans.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny grazers of phytoplankton in the estuary, and food for young hilsa.

nodes.name: Hilsa
nodes.desc: A plankton-feeding fish that lives in estuaries and swims up rivers to spawn. It is Bangladesh's national fish.

nodes.name: Mudskippers
nodes.desc: Amphibious fish that hop across exposed mudflats at low tide and eat small invertebrates.

nodes.name: Fishing cat
nodes.desc: A wetland cat that ambushes prey at the water's edge. Fish are its main food, with crabs and rodents also taken.

nodes.name: Water monitor
nodes.desc: A large lizard that forages along creeks and mudflats. Tiger remains in the Sundarbans have included water monitors.

nodes.name: White-bellied sea eagle
nodes.desc: A coastal raptor that takes fish about half of its diet, and also hunts waterbirds and reptiles. Nests in tall trees by water.

nodes.name: Irrawaddy dolphin
nodes.desc: A small dolphin of the Sundarbans waterways that hunts fish and shrimp in brackish water.

nodes.name: Ganges river dolphin
nodes.desc: A freshwater dolphin that lives in the less salty channels and hunts fish and shrimp.

nodes.name: Bengal tiger
nodes.desc: The only tigers living in mangroves. They swim between islands and eat deer, boar, fish, crabs and monitors.

nodes.name: Saltwater crocodile
nodes.desc: An ambush predator that eats mud crabs, fish and large mammals such as deer and boar.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Powers photosynthesis in the trees and the algae.

nodes.name: Tidal salinity
nodes.desc: Tides and the balance of fresh and salt water set which trees survive. Rising sea level and less river flow push salt further inland.

nodes.name: Delta silt & nutrients
nodes.desc: The Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna deliver mud and nutrients that feed the forest and the tidal flats.

nodes.name: Mud bacteria & fungi
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves and dead animals in the tidal mud, returning nutrients to the forest.
